questions.q: Where does the user_id -> subscriber_id rename happen, and why there specifically?
options: In the staging layer, so the two source systems' naming is reconciled once instead of re-derived differently in every downstream model or report
In Power BI, where each report author can decide independently
It happens automatically; dbt detects matching entities without any explicit rename
In the marts layer, after all joins are complete
questions.explain: Reconciling naming differences once in staging avoids it being re-derived inconsistently downstream -- the core reason staging exists as its own layer.

questions.q: What is the first model in this dbt project where billing and usage data actually get joined together?
options: int_subscriber_activity (the intermediate model)
stg_billing_events (a staging model)
dim_subscribers (a mart)
The raw source tables themselves
questions.explain: Staging models clean one source at a time with no joins; the intermediate model is where billing and usage data first meet.

questions.q: Why does this project use {{ ref('stg_billing_events') }} instead of a hardcoded schema.table reference?
options: ref() lets dbt automatically build the project's dependency graph and run models in the correct order
ref() is purely stylistic and has no functional effect
Hardcoded references are faster to execute
ref() is required only for staging models, not intermediate ones
questions.explain: ref() is what allows dbt to understand and automatically order the model dependency graph -- a hardcoded table name wouldn't give dbt that information.

questions.q: What does try_to_decimal() do differently from a plain CAST when converting a malformed amount_usd value?
options: It converts without throwing an error, turning a bad value into a visible NULL a dbt test can catch, instead of failing the whole pipeline run
It automatically fixes the malformed value to a best guess
It behaves identically to CAST with no difference
It silently drops the row entirely
questions.explain: try_to_decimal() (and try_to_timestamp_ntz()) fail gracefully into NULL rather than erroring out the whole statement -- making bad data visible and testable instead of breaking the run.

questions.q: What is the fact/dimension split used in the marts layer here?
options: fct_subscriptions (one row per subscription event) and dim_subscribers (one row per subscriber)
Both tables contain identical data for redundancy
There is only one mart table, combining facts and dimensions
dim_subscribers contains events and fct_subscriptions contains subscriber attributes
questions.explain: fct_subscriptions is the fact table (event-grain) and dim_subscribers is the dimension table (subscriber-grain) -- the same fact/dimension split taught in the dbt and Power BI courses.
